patch_description:
Replace the final coordinate polishing stage with a plateau-aware hard max-min refinement. The previous polish selected only the largest immediate minimum area, so when many proposals tied at the current bottleneck it almost always retained proposal zero (the current point), preventing motion along the common flat faces of the nonsmooth Heilbronn objective.

The new refinement uses denser, phase-rotated radial proposals and permits only moves that do not reduce the strict current minimum. Among those feasible plateau moves, it selects the configuration with the strongest lower tail (sum of the 18 smallest triangle areas). This is a deterministic lexicographic-style refinement: preserve the actual evaluated objective first, then improve near-active constraints so later moves can raise the bottleneck. Rotating the proposal stencil by an irrational phase avoids repeatedly searching only the same coordinate directions.
